info.description: OpenAI-compatible inference API for DiCompute. Point an OpenAI SDK at the server URL below and keep your client. Authenticate with `Authorization: Bearer <api-key>`; see the authentication guide linked from `components.securitySchemes`. Note that the authenticated routes send no CORS headers and are intended for server-side clients. One status code is a documented exception to the error envelope every operation below declares: `429` (rate limiting). An application-level rate limit answers 429 in the same JSON envelope as every other error, but the same paths can also receive a 429 from an edge (Cloudflare) rule that answers `content-type: text/html` instead (DICOMPUTE/Open, public issue 770) -- so no operation below declares a typed 429 response; treat any 429 as retryable and parse its body defensively.

post.summary: Run a chat completion, streaming or not.
post.description: OpenAI-compatible. Accepts the same `messages` array any OpenAI SDK sends. Set `stream: true` for a server-sent-events response identical in shape to OpenAI's own streaming format -- the same client code that works against api.openai.com works here with one base-URL change. Send an optional `Idempotency-Key` header to retry safely -- a dropped connection can't tell you whether the request billed, and this lets a retry find out instead of guessing. Same key + same request body within 24h replays the ORIGINAL response verbatim (tagged `Idempotency-Replayed: true`) and bills nothing a second time; the same key with a different body is rejected (422), and two concurrent requests sharing a key resolve as one success and one 409, never two charges. Scoped to your account, so a key you reuse is never visible to (or replayable by) any other account. Not supported on a streaming request (`stream: true`) -- a partially-delivered SSE stream can't be replayed honestly, so a keyed streaming request is refused (422) rather than silently ignoring the key. Send optional `HTTP-Referer` and `X-DiCompute-Title` headers to identify YOUR app -- the same convention OpenRouter uses for its app rankings. Only the referer's host is stored (never the path or query string); both headers are decoration, never validation, so an absent or malformed value changes nothing about the response. Attributed usage feeds the public app leaderboard (GET /v1/stats/apps) once your app clears its minimum-activity floor. Every inference response -- streaming or not -- also carries an `x-dico-cache-status: hit | miss | bypass` response header. Non-stream, it is sourced from the same `cached_tokens` count billing records on the settle receipt, so it can never contradict what you were charged: `hit` means the engine reported cached prompt tokens (billed at the discounted cache-read rate), and `bypass` is the honest value while the exact-prefix rollout is disabled -- every deployment of this codebase today. On a stream the header is stamped when the response headers flush, BEFORE the usage frame carrying `cached_tokens` exists, so it reports the flush-time truth (`bypass` today, `miss` once the rollout is enabled) and can never claim `hit` -- a streamed response's per-request cache signal is `usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens` on the terminal usage frame instead. Do not conflate this with the `x-cache-status` header on GET /v1/cache/status: that one reports the deployment-wide rollout state (`enabled | disabled`), this one reports a per-response outcome.

post.summary: Score documents against a query with a cross-encoder, most relevant first.
post.description: `documents[].index` in the response is ALWAYS the position the document held in YOUR `documents` array, never the position in the sorted result -- look a scored document back up by that index, not by counting through the response. Omit `top_n` to get every document scored; set it to get only the top N. Set `return_documents: true` to have each result echo its own document text back (otherwise only the index and score are returned). Supports an optional `Idempotency-Key` header, same replay/conflict/body-mismatch contract as `/v1/chat/completions` (see that endpoint's own description).

post.summary: Embed text into a vector, for a model your operator has explicitly configured for it.
post.description: OpenAI-compatible. `model` must be one this deployment has declared `capabilities.embedding: true` for -- GET /openai/v1/models reports that flag per model, same as it reports `capabilities.vision`/`tools`. A model that exists but was never declared embedding-capable (every chat model, in a default deployment) answers `model_not_found` (400) -- this route never silently serves a chat model's output as an "embedding". `input` accepts either a single string or a batch (array of strings, up to 2048 items); a failed upstream call refunds the reservation in full and settles no charge -- the same fail-closed discipline /v1/chat/completions applies. the Idempotency-Key contract carries over unchanged: same key + same body replays the original response and bills nothing a second time.

post.summary: Ingest a document -- chunked, embedded, and stored.
post.description: Requires a spending key with inference scope -- this lowers to /v1/embeddings and bills exactly as if you had called it directly (a browsing session alone is refused). `content_type` is `text/plain`, `text/markdown`, `application/pdf`, or the DOCX mime type; a PDF/DOCX's `content` is base64 with `content_encoding: "base64"` -- bytes are sniffed and content-scanned, never trusted off the declared type. A document whose extracted text is long enough ingests asynchronously: `status` comes back `"pending"` (202) instead of `"ready"` (201), and later requests on this document reflect the same status once the queue drains.

post.summary: Extract plain text from an uploaded PDF, DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, or ZIP -- never truncated silently.
post.description: The raw file bytes ARE the request body -- not JSON, not multipart. Content-Type is never inspected; the actual bytes are classified by magic number (plus, for the four ZIP-container formats, an inner marker entry -- see blob-sniff.ts's `sniffDocumentType`), so a mislabeled or extension-renamed file is refused on its real bytes, not its claimed type. Legacy binary `.doc`/`.xls`/`.ppt` and non-ZIP archives (`.rar`, `.7z`, `.tar.gz`) are not supported and are refused the same way an unrecognized format is. Capped at 4 MiB raw upload (operator-tunable, `API_MAX_BLOB_UPLOAD_BYTES`; 413 `request_too_large` over that). A fixed per-extraction cost (10, 000 µUSD by default, `EXTRACT_TEXT_COST_UUSD`) is charged after the type is sniffed but before any CPU-intensive work runs -- insufficient balance is 402 `insufficient_balance`, charged once regardless of whether the extraction itself then succeeds. At most 5 extractions run at once on this deployment (`EXTRACT_TEXT_MAX_CONCURRENT`) -- over that, this route fails fast with 429 `concurrency_limited` rather than queueing, since a queued extraction would still cost the same CPU later. A PDF's own text is bounded further: at most 500 pages are read, extracted text is capped at 66,000 characters (**refused as a specific field, never silently truncated past that point -- `truncated_from_chars` on the response reports the real original length when it is**), and extraction is torn down by a real OS-thread `Worker.terminate` if it has not finished in 10 seconds (504 `extraction_timeout`) -- a same-thread timer cannot preempt a hostile PDF's own synchronous parse, which is why this is a real worker kill, not a race against a timer. DOCX/XLSX/PPTX/ZIP extraction shares the identical 66,000-character extracted-text cap (no page cap or wall-clock timeout of their own -- decompression itself is bounded instead, see docx-extract.ts's own header). A document with no extractable text at all (encrypted, scanned/image-only, corrupt, or genuinely empty) is `422 no_text_layer` -- one honest reason covering every one of those causes, because this route cannot reliably tell them apart. Nothing this route reads is ever stored or logged beyond a byte count and a character count -- the document's own bytes and extracted text are never written to disk or to a log line.
